b1-hifil.title: Hifil Verbs: מַזְמִין, הִזְמַנְתִּי
b1-hifil.pattern: present מַ…ִי · past הִ…ְ…ַ · future אַ…ִי · infinitive לְהַ…ִי
b1-hifil.explanation: Hifil verbs often mean 'to make something happen'. Present starts with מַ (מַזְמִין, 'invites, orders'), past with הִ (הִזְמַנְתִּי, 'I invited'), future with אַ / תַּ / יַ (אַזְמִין, 'I will invite'), and the infinitive with לְהַ (לְהַזְמִין). Common ones: מַתְחִיל (starts), מַרְגִּישׁ (feels), מַסְבִּיר (explains), מַמְלִיץ (recommends).
b1-hifil.fact: Many hifil verbs come from the same root as a simpler verb: גָּדַל 'grew' → הִגְדִּיל 'enlarged'; לָבַשׁ 'wore' → הִלְבִּישׁ 'dressed someone'.

dialogue.en: Have you already booked a table?

b1-nifal.title: Nifal: Things That Happen
b1-nifal.pattern: נִפְתַּח (was opened, opens) · נִסְגַּר · נִכְנַס · נִשְׁאַר
b1-nifal.explanation: Nifal verbs start with נִ in the past (נִפְתַּח, 'opened / was opened') and the present (נִפְתָּח). They are often passive or 'happening by itself': הַדֶּלֶת נִסְגְּרָה ('the door closed'). Some everyday verbs live only here: נִכְנַס (entered), נִשְׁאַר (stayed), נִפְגַּשׁ (met), נִרְדַּם (fell asleep).
b1-nifal.fact: The infinitive of nifal starts with לְהִ and has a dagesh in the first root letter: לְהִכָּנֵס (to enter), לְהִפָּגֵשׁ (to meet).

dialogue.en: Let's meet next to the cinema.

b1-would.title: I Would…: הָיִיתִי + present
b1-would.pattern: הָיִיתִי רוֹצֶה (I would like) · אִלּוּ… הָיִיתִי…
b1-would.explanation: 'Would' is the past of 'to be' + a present-tense verb: הָיִיתִי רוֹצֶה ('I would like'), הוּא הָיָה בָּא ('he would come'). For imagined situations use אִם or the more formal אִלּוּ: אִם הָיָה לִי כֶּסֶף, הָיִיתִי נוֹסֵעַ ('if I had money, I would travel').
b1-would.fact: הָיִיתִי רוֹצֶה / רוֹצָה is the polite way to order or ask for something, a step up from אֲנִי רוֹצֶה.

dialogue.native: מָה הָיִיתָ עוֹשֶׂה עִם מִילְיוֹן שֶׁקֶל?
dialogue.en: What would you do with a million shekels?
I'd buy a house by the sea.

b1-kdei.title: In Order To and So That
b1-kdei.pattern: כְּדֵי לְ… (in order to) · כְּדֵי שֶׁ… + future (so that)
b1-kdei.explanation: 'In order to' is כְּדֵי + infinitive: אֲנִי לוֹמֵד כְּדֵי לַעֲבֹד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל. When the subject changes, use כְּדֵי שֶׁ + future: אֲנִי מַסְבִּיר לְאַט כְּדֵי שֶׁתָּבִין ('I explain slowly so that you understand').
b1-kdei.fact: In everyday speech you will also hear בִּשְׁבִיל לְ… with the same meaning as כְּדֵי לְ…

dialogue.native: לָמָּה אַתָּה קָם כָּל כָּךְ מֻקְדָּם?
dialogue.en: Why do you get up so early?

b1-reported.title: He Said That…: Reported Speech
b1-reported.pattern: הוּא אָמַר שֶׁ… · הִיא שָׁאֲלָה אִם… · הֵם סִפְּרוּ שֶׁ…
b1-reported.explanation: Reported speech in Hebrew is simple: keep the original tense. If Dana said 'I'm tired', you report דָּנָה אָמְרָה שֶׁהִיא עֲיֵפָה ('Dana said that she is tired'), with no change to the past. Yes/no questions are reported with אִם ('whether'): הוּא שָׁאַל אִם אֲנִי בָּא.
b1-reported.fact: This is a common mistake for English speakers: don't shift the tense. 'He said he would come' is הוּא אָמַר שֶׁהוּא יָבוֹא — future, not past.

dialogue.en: He said he'll be a bit late.

b1-opinion.title: Giving Your Opinion
b1-opinion.pattern: לְדַעֲתִי · אֲנִי חוֹשֵׁב שֶׁ… · אֲנִי מַסְכִּים / לֹא מַסְכִּים
b1-opinion.explanation: Opinions: לְדַעֲתִי ('in my opinion'), אֲנִי חוֹשֵׁב / חוֹשֶׁבֶת שֶׁ… ('I think that'), נִרְאֶה לִי שֶׁ… ('it seems to me'). Agree with אֲנִי מַסְכִּים עִם… or simply נָכוֹן ('right'). Disagree politely: אֲנִי לֹא בָּטוּחַ ('I'm not sure') or יֵשׁ בָּזֶה מַשֶּׁהוּ, אֲבָל… ('there's something in that, but…').
b1-opinion.fact: Israeli conversation is known for being direct: interrupting to disagree is normal, and nobody takes it personally.

dialogue.en: In my opinion the film was boring.

dialogue.native: אֲנִי לֹא מַסְכִּים, הוּא הָיָה מְעַנְיֵן!

b1-interview.title: A Job Interview
b1-interview.explanation: Useful words: רֵאָיוֹן עֲבוֹדָה (job interview), קוֹרוֹת חַיִּים (CV, 'the events of life'), נִסָּיוֹן (experience), מַשְׂכֹּרֶת (salary), מִשְׂרָה מְלֵאָה / חֶלְקִית (full-time / part-time job). Talk about experience with יֵשׁ לִי נִסָּיוֹן בְּ… and with עָבַדְתִּי בְּ… שְׁנָתַיִם ('I worked at… for two years').
b1-interview.fact: Israeli interviews are often informal; you may be asked about your army service, which many employers treat as work experience.

dialogue.en: I worked for three years at a big company.

b1-bank.title: Money and the Bank
b1-bank.pattern: חֶשְׁבּוֹן בַּנְק · כַּרְטִיס אַשְׁרַאי · לְהַעֲבִיר כֶּסֶף
b1-bank.explanation: Banking words: חֶשְׁבּוֹן בַּנְק (bank account), כַּרְטִיס אַשְׁרַאי (credit card), לִמְשֹׁךְ כֶּסֶף (to withdraw money), לְהַעֲבִיר כֶּסֶף (to transfer money), תַּשְׁלוּמִים (instalments). Israelis often split purchases into instalments, even small ones: בְּכַמָּה תַּשְׁלוּמִים? ('in how many payments?').
b1-bank.fact: The ATM is called כַּסְפּוֹמָט, a blend of כֶּסֶף ('money') and 'automat'.

b1-complaint.title: Complaining Politely
b1-complaint.pattern: יֵשׁ לִי בְּעָיָה עִם… · זֶה לֹא עוֹבֵד · אֶפְשָׁר לְהַחְלִיף?
b1-complaint.explanation: To complain: יֵשׁ לִי בְּעָיָה עִם… ('I have a problem with'), זֶה לֹא עוֹבֵד ('it doesn't work'), זֶה מְקֻלְקָל ('it's broken'). Ask for a fix: אֶפְשָׁר לְהַחְלִיף? ('can I exchange it?'), אֶפְשָׁר לְקַבֵּל אֶת הַכֶּסֶף בַּחֲזָרָה? ('can I get my money back?'). Keep the receipt: קַבָּלָה.
b1-complaint.fact: Israeli shops must accept returns within 14 days for many goods, but only with the receipt.

dialogue.native: קָנִיתִי אֶת זֶה אֶתְמוֹל וְזֶה לֹא עוֹבֵד.
dialogue.en: I bought this yesterday and it doesn't work.

b1-tech.title: Phones and Computers
b1-tech.explanation: Tech words: מַחְשֵׁב (computer), סִסְמָה (password), לְהוֹרִיד (to download, 'to bring down'), לְהַעֲלוֹת (to upload, 'to bring up'), מִטְעָן (charger), הַסּוֹלְלָה נִגְמְרָה ('the battery died'), אֵין קְלִיטָה ('no signal'). Many words are borrowed: אַפְּלִיקַצְיָה, אִינְטֶרְנֶט.
b1-tech.fact: Israel is famous for start-ups: the country has one of the highest numbers of start-ups per person in the world.

b1-cooking.title: In the Kitchen
b1-cooking.explanation: Recipes (מַתְכּוֹנִים) are usually written with infinitives as instructions: לַחְתֹּךְ אֶת הַבָּצָל ('chop the onion'), לְעַרְבֵּב ('mix'), לְהוֹסִיף ('add'), לְבַשֵּׁל עַל אֵשׁ קְטַנָּה ('cook on a low heat'), לֶאֱפוֹת בַּתַּנּוּר ('bake in the oven').
b1-cooking.fact: שַׁקְשׁוּקָה — eggs cooked in a spicy tomato sauce — came to Israel with immigrants from North Africa and is now a national breakfast.

b1-travel.title: Travelling Abroad
b1-travel.explanation: Abroad is חוּ"ל, short for חוּץ לָאָרֶץ ('outside the land'). At the airport: דַּרְכּוֹן (passport), טִיסָה (flight), מִזְוָדָה (suitcase), כַּרְטִיס עֲלִיָּה לַמָּטוֹס (boarding pass). Flights 'go up' and 'land': הַמָּטוֹס הִמְרִיא ('took off'), נָחַת ('landed').
b1-travel.fact: Israel's main airport, Ben Gurion, is known for long security questioning before departure.

dialogue.native: מָחָר בְּשֵׁשׁ בַּבֹּקֶר, אֲנִי עוֹד לֹא אָרַזְתִּי!
dialogue.en: Tomorrow at six in the morning, I haven't packed yet!

b1-news.title: In the News
b1-news.pattern: חֲדָשׁוֹת · לְפִי הַדִּוּוּחַ · הַמֶּמְשָׁלָה · מֶזֶג הָאֲוִיר
b1-news.explanation: News Hebrew uses some fixed phrases: לְפִי… ('according to'), הַיּוֹם נִמְסַר שֶׁ… ('it was reported today that'), בְּעִקְבוֹת ('following, as a result of'). Common words: הַמֶּמְשָׁלָה (the government), בְּחִירוֹת (elections), תְּאֻנָּה (accident), שְׁבִיתָה (strike), תַּחֲזִית (forecast).
b1-news.fact: Many Israeli radio stations still play the news on the hour, and people in a shared taxi often ask the driver to turn it up.

dialogue.en: Yes, there's a train strike tomorrow.

b1-environment.title: The Environment
b1-environment.explanation: Environment words: הַסְּבִיבָה (the environment), מִחְזוּר (recycling), זִהוּם (pollution), אֶנֶרְגִּיָה מֵהַשֶּׁמֶשׁ (solar energy), לַחְסֹךְ מַיִם (to save water), שִׁנּוּי אַקְלִים (climate change).
b1-environment.fact: Israel recycles most of its waste water for farming, one of the highest rates in the world, because fresh water is scarce.

dialogue.en: Yes, we have a bin for bottles.

b1-sport.title: Sport and Free Time
b1-sport.explanation: Free time: תַּחְבִּיב (hobby), לְשַׂחֵק כַּדּוּרֶגֶל / כַּדּוּרְסַל (to play football / basketball), לִשְׂחוֹת (to swim), לָרוּץ (to run), לְטַיֵּל (to hike, to travel around). 'A fan of' is אוֹהֵד שֶׁל…, and a match is מִשְׂחָק.
b1-sport.fact: טִיּוּל ('a trip, a hike') is a national pastime: many Israelis go on a long backpacking trip after the army.

dialogue.en: I love hiking in the north.

b1-army.title: Israeli Life: Army and Studies
b1-army.explanation: Most young Israelis do military service (שֵׁרוּת צְבָאִי) at 18 — about three years for men and two for women — and afterwards many are called up for reserve duty (מִלּוּאִים) for some weeks a year. University (אוּנִיבֶרְסִיטָה) usually comes after the army; a degree is תּוֹאַר, a first degree תּוֹאַר רִאשׁוֹן.
b1-army.fact: Because they start later, Israeli students are often in their mid-twenties, and many already work while studying.

dialogue.en: What did you do after the army?
I travelled in India and then started studying.
